attempts.summary: Created an Ansible playbook (run from node1 as the control node) that provisions an opsbot account on node1 and node2, generates an ed25519 SSH keypair for opsbot on node1, authorizes that public key on node2, and enforces key-only SSH authentication for opsbot on both nodes via a `Match User opsbot` sshd drop-in (PasswordAuthentication no, AuthenticationMethods publickey). Verified opsbot@node1 can SSH into opsbot@node2 and run commands, and that password auth is rejected for opsbot on both nodes. Also had to fix node2's SSH server, which had no host keys and was never started (dpkg-reconfigure openssh-server + enable ssh) before Ansible could reach it over SSH. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for node1, node2, and node3, proving changed boot IDs and post-restart recovery of the opsbot SSH setup.
